source: NutriLens Clinical and Hormonal Nutrition Protocols

diet_plans.name: PCOS & Hormone Balance Diet
diet_plans.tagline: Evidence-informed nutrition for insulin sensitivity and androgen balance
diet_plans.description: Helps manage insulin resistance, support ovulatory health, and moderate androgen influence using local Bangladeshi anti-inflammatory foods.
diet_plans.fullOverview: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) involves underlying hyperinsulinemia driving excess ovarian androgen production. This protocol prioritizes complex low-GI carbohydrates (Red rice, Besan, Lentils), anti-inflammatory local fish, and spearmint tea to support endocrine balance.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Individuals with PCOS or metabolic-hormonal irregularity

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: Low-GI complex carbohydrates reduce postprandial insulin surges, lowering insulin-mediated ovarian androgen synthesis. Spearmint and flaxseeds provide mild anti-androgenic and phytoestrogenic support.

keyBenefits: Low glycemic load prevents acute insulin surges
Rich in omega-3 and plant lignans for hormone balance
High dietary fiber promotes satiety and gut clearance of metabolites
guidelines: Begin mornings with a warm cup of spearmint tea and soaked chia or flaxseeds.
Ensure half your lunch plate consists of fiber-rich cooked vegetables or shak.
Avoid skipping breakfast to maintain stable morning cortisol and insulin levels.

sampleMealDay.breakfast: 2 Besan/oats chillas with grated bottle gourd + 1 boiled egg + unsweetened spearmint tea
sampleMealDay.lunch: 1 small cup Red rice (Lal chal) + Palong shak bhaji + Rui fish curry with light gravy + Cucumber salad
sampleMealDay.dinner: 1 handmade multigrain roti + Boiled mixed dal + Stir-fried pointed gourd (potol) and chicken breast
sampleMealDay.snack: A handful of roasted pumpkin seeds + 1 cup warm green tea with cinnamon

diet_plans.name: Hypothyroidism Metabolic Nutrition Protocol
diet_plans.tagline: Micronutrient-targeted nutrition to support thyroid hormone synthesis and metabolic rate
diet_plans.description: Supplies bioavailable Selenium, Zinc, and Iodine while minimizing raw goitrogens to support resting metabolic energy.
diet_plans.fullOverview: Hypothyroidism can lower basal metabolic rate and impair gut motility. This protocol incorporates marine fish, pumpkin seeds, and cooked leafy greens to support deiodinase enzyme conversion of T4 to active T3.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Individuals with underactive thyroid (elevated TSH) or low metabolic rate

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: Selenium and Zinc act as essential cofactors for 5'-deiodinase enzymes that convert T4 to active T3. Cooking cruciferous vegetables inactivates myrosinase, ensuring safe intake.
potential_benefits: Aids gut motility and fluid clearance

keyBenefits: Rich in bioavailable Selenium and Zinc for enzymatic conversion
High soluble fiber to support sluggish bowel transit
Guidance on separating meals from Levothyroxine medication by 60 minutes
foodsToLimit: Raw cabbage and cauliflower (cook thoroughly instead)
guidelines: Take thyroid medication on an empty stomach with plain water at least 45-60 minutes before breakfast.
Always cook cruciferous vegetables (cabbage, cauliflower) thoroughly to neutralize goitrogenic activity.
Snack on a tablespoon of roasted pumpkin seeds for daily zinc and magnesium.

sampleMealDay.breakfast: 2 whole eggs scrambled with tomatoes + 1 slice whole-wheat toast + 1 glass lukewarm lemon water
sampleMealDay.lunch: 1 cup Red rice + Cooked loitta or rupchanda fish with ginger turmeric gravy + Lau shak + Cucumber salad
sampleMealDay.dinner: Vegetable and chicken soup with bottle gourd and carrots + 1 small handmade roti
sampleMealDay.snack: 1 cup Tok doi (yogurt) sprinkled with 1 tbsp roasted pumpkin seeds

diet_plans.name: Deshi Low-GI Insulin Resistance Protocol
diet_plans.tagline: Controlled glycemic load nutrition to improve insulin sensitivity and energy balance
diet_plans.description: Focuses on high-amylose grains, legumes, and lean protein to prevent rapid postprandial glycemic excursions.
diet_plans.fullOverview: Insulin resistance impairs cellular glucose uptake and promotes visceral fat accumulation. This protocol utilizes fiber-dense Bangladeshi staples like Lal atta, chola, and bitter gourd (karela) to smooth glucose curves.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Individuals with prediabetes, central adiposity, or elevated fasting insulin

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: High-fiber complex carbohydrates and resistant starches slow gastric emptying and enzymatic starch hydrolysis, moderating postprandial glucose excursions.
potential_benefits: Supports stable energy levels throughout the day

keyBenefits: Reduces glycemic excursions without severe carbohydrate starvation
High satiety indices preventing late-night binge eating
Cardio-metabolic support with bioactive polyphenols
guidelines: Follow the Plate Method: 1/2 non-starchy vegetables, 1/4 lean protein, 1/4 quality low-GI carbohydrate.
Incorporate a 10-minute gentle post-meal walk to activate GLUT-4 glucose uptake without insulin.
Drink a glass of water with 1 tsp soaked isabgol 15 minutes before lunch.

sampleMealDay.breakfast: 2 small Lal atta rotis + Boiled chickpeas with tomato and cucumber + 1 boiled egg
sampleMealDay.lunch: 1 cup Red rice or 2 rotis + Karela bhaji + Katla fish curry + Thick dal + Lemon salad
sampleMealDay.dinner: Grilled deshi chicken breast + Steamed mixed vegetables (potol, dharosh, lau) + 1 small roti
sampleMealDay.snack: 1 cup black coffee or green tea + 15 roasted unsalted almonds

diet_plans.name: DASH Cardio Care & Blood Pressure Protocol
diet_plans.tagline: Potassium-rich, mineral-balanced protocol supporting arterial elasticity and cardiovascular health
diet_plans.description: Emphasizes dietary potassium, magnesium, and calcium while moderating sodium to support blood pressure management.
diet_plans.fullOverview: Modeled after the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) framework, this protocol integrates local potassium sources like green coconut water, bananas, and leafy greens to support vascular tone.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Individuals managing high blood pressure or prioritizing cardiovascular health

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: High dietary potassium and magnesium intake promotes vasodilation and natriuresis, mitigating the hypertensive effects of excess dietary sodium.
potential_benefits: Supports healthy systolic and diastolic blood pressure

keyBenefits: AHA-aligned sodium management working toward ≤1,500 mg/day when appropriate
Rich in potassium, magnesium, and calcium from natural foods
Zero artificial trans-fats or high-sodium seasonings
guidelines: Do not add extra table salt to your rice or salad plate.
Flavor dishes with lemon juice, fresh ginger, garlic, and cumin instead of excess salt.
Enjoy a glass of fresh green coconut water 2-3 times weekly for natural potassium.

sampleMealDay.breakfast: 1 bowl oats cooked in low-fat milk + Sliced banana and 10 unsalted almonds + 1 boiled egg white
sampleMealDay.lunch: 1 cup brown or red rice + Rui fish cooked with tomato and cumin + Palong shak bhaji with garlic + Sliced cucumber
sampleMealDay.dinner: 2 whole wheat rotis + Mixed vegetable curry (beans, carrots, potato) + 1 cup yellow lentil soup (dal)
sampleMealDay.snack: 1 glass fresh green coconut water or 1 fresh guava

diet_plans.name: Fatty Liver (NAFLD) Lifestyle Nutrition Protocol
diet_plans.tagline: Hepatic lipid reduction and antioxidant support through sulfur-rich vegetables and low fructose
diet_plans.description: Nutritional lifestyle support designed to reduce hepatic triglyceride accumulation and oxidative stress.
diet_plans.fullOverview: Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease (NAFLD) is characterized by hepatic de novo lipogenesis driven by refined carbohydrates and fructose. This protocol emphasizes cruciferous vegetables, fresh garlic, green tea, and lean fish to support liver cellular health.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Individuals with Grade 1 or 2 fatty liver, elevated ALT/AST, or metabolic syndrome

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: Limiting refined carbohydrates and fructose reduces hepatic substrate availability for de novo lipogenesis, while sulfur compounds (allicin, sulforaphane) support Phase II liver detox pathways.
potential_benefits: Supports reduction of intrahepatic fat accumulation
Helps normalize ALT and AST transaminases

keyBenefits: Eliminates high-fructose corn syrup and refined sweeteners
Rich in sulfur-rich allicin (garlic) and sulforaphane (crucifers)
Supplies EGCG from green tea to support hepatic lipid oxidation
foodsToLimit: Commercial fruit juices and soft drinks
guidelines: Drink 2 cups of freshly brewed unsweetened green tea daily for antioxidant EGCG.
Include 1-2 crushed fresh garlic cloves in your daily meals for allicin benefits.
Eliminate all packaged juices, sweetened drinks, and artificial syrups.

sampleMealDay.breakfast: 2 scrambled egg whites + 1 slice whole wheat bread + 1 cup green tea with lemon
sampleMealDay.lunch: 1 cup Red rice + Steamed Rui fish with garlic turmeric sauce + Cooked broccoli and cauliflower + Lemon salad
sampleMealDay.dinner: Clear chicken and vegetable soup with ginger and garlic + 1 small roti
sampleMealDay.snack: 1/2 cup Tok doi with a pinch of black pepper and roasted cumin

diet_plans.name: Low-Purine Uric Acid & Gout Care Protocol
diet_plans.tagline: Purine-conscious nutrition and alkaline hydration to support healthy uric acid clearance
diet_plans.description: Balances portion sizes of purine-containing foods while providing alkalizing vegetables and ample hydration.
diet_plans.fullOverview: Hyperuricemia occurs when uric acid production exceeds renal excretion. This protocol replaces high-purine organ meats and selected seafood with moderate proteins like eggs and low-fat dairy while encouraging high water intake.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Individuals managing high blood uric acid (>6.0 mg/dL in females, >7.0 mg/dL in males) or gouty flare-ups

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: Limiting high-purine cellular substrates reduces exogenous xanthine oxidase degradation into uric acid, while low-fat dairy and vitamin C promote renal urate clearance.
potential_benefits: Helps reduce the frequency of painful joint flare-ups

keyBenefits: Portion-aware management of moderate-purine fresh fish
High dietary hydration target (>3,000 ml/day) to prevent crystal crystallization
Emphasis on eggs and low-fat dairy for safe protein
allowedFoods: Red rice and Lal atta roti
guidelines: Drink at least 3.0 to 3.5 liters of clean water daily to facilitate renal uric acid clearance.
Rely on whole eggs, low-fat yogurt, and light fish portions (under 100g) for protein.
Avoid red meat, beef liver, and dried fish (shutki) during active joint swelling.

sampleMealDay.breakfast: 2 whole boiled eggs + 2 slices brown bread + Cucumber and tomato slices + 1 large glass water with lemon
sampleMealDay.lunch: 1 cup Red rice + Bottle gourd (Lau) curry + 1 small piece Rui fish (approx 80g) + 1 cup Tok doi
sampleMealDay.dinner: 2 handmade rotis + Steamed pointed gourd and pumpkin curry + 1 bowl light vegetable soup
sampleMealDay.snack: 1 fresh guava or apple + 2 glasses of water

diet_plans.name: Anti-Inflammatory Fertility Prep Diet
diet_plans.tagline: Micronutrient-dense protocol to support ovulatory function and cellular health
diet_plans.description: Enriched with dietary Folate, Omega-3 fatty acids, and antioxidants to support reproductive vitality.
diet_plans.fullOverview: Chronic low-grade inflammation can affect reproductive health. This protocol utilizes pomegranate, walnuts, golden turmeric milk, and local greens to provide comprehensive micronutrient nourishment.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Individuals planning pregnancy or seeking reproductive nutritional support

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: Antioxidants (polyphenols, vitamins C and E) mitigate follicular oxidative stress, while omega-3s and folate support cellular division and endometrial receptivity.

keyBenefits: High dietary folate from natural greens and legumes
Omega-3 fatty acids for anti-inflammatory eicosanoid balance
Rich in colorful polyphenols and carotenoids
foodsToLimit: Artificial trans fats and hydrogenated dalda
guidelines: Include a handful of pomegranate seeds or fresh guava daily for antioxidant support.
Ensure daily intake of natural folate from dark leafy greens and boiled lentils.
Limit commercial coffee and tea to no more than 1 cup daily.

sampleMealDay.breakfast: 2 whole eggs with spinach omelet + 1 slice whole wheat bread + 1/2 cup pomegranate seeds
sampleMealDay.lunch: 1 cup Red rice + Tengra fish curry with tomatoes + Methi shak bhaji + Dal
sampleMealDay.dinner: 1 handmade roti + Grilled chicken breast + Steamed broccoli and carrots
sampleMealDay.snack: Warm low-fat milk with a pinch of turmeric and 4 walnuts

diet_plans.name: Targeted Deshi Keto Protocol
diet_plans.tagline: Controlled low-carbohydrate nutritional protocol utilizing authentic Bangladeshi staples
diet_plans.description: Shifts primary metabolic fuel from glucose to ketone bodies through high-quality deshi fats and proteins.
diet_plans.fullOverview: A targeted ketogenic approach adapted for Bangladeshi dietary patterns using pure ghee, mustard oil, eggs, deshi fish, and green leafy vegetables while keeping daily net carbohydrates under 30g.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Individuals seeking rapid insulin reduction or accustomed to ketogenic eating

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: Limiting carbohydrate intake below 30g/day depletes hepatic glycogen stores, stimulating beta-oxidation and ketogenesis.
potential_benefits: Rapid reduction in circulating insulin levels
Significant reduction in hunger and snacking urges
Efficient fat loss when calories are controlled

keyBenefits: Very low net carbohydrate intake (<30g daily)
Nutritious local healthy fats (Deshi Ghee, Mustard oil)
Zero starvation or constant hunger pangs
guidelines: Maintain electrolyte balance by drinking mineralized water with a pinch of Himalayan pink salt.
Eat plenty of leafy greens (Palong and Kolmi shak) to support digestion and magnesium levels.
Strictly avoid cheat meals during initial adaptation to maintain nutritional ketosis.

sampleMealDay.breakfast: 3 whole eggs fried in 1 tbsp pure ghee + Sliced cucumber + Black coffee with 1 tsp ghee/MCT
sampleMealDay.lunch: Rui fish cooked in mustard oil + 1 large bowl sautéed Palong shak with green chillies + Sliced cucumber
sampleMealDay.dinner: Deshi chicken curry in rich spicy ghee gravy + 1 large bowl cauliflower rice + Green salad
sampleMealDay.snack: A handful of roasted salted almonds or walnuts

diet_plans.name: Hormone-Safe Intermittent Fasting (14/10)
diet_plans.tagline: Gentle 14-hour fasting protocol designed to protect adrenal and thyroid hormone rhythms
diet_plans.description: Improves cellular autophagy and insulin sensitivity without the cortisol spikes associated with extreme 18+ hour fasts.
diet_plans.fullOverview: Extreme prolonged fasting can trigger stress responses in sensitive endocrine systems. A moderate 14-hour overnight fast with a 10-hour eating window provides metabolic benefits while keeping cortisol and leptin balanced.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Individuals seeking sustainable time-restricted eating without adrenal burnout

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: A 14-hour overnight fast allows hepatic glycogen mobilization and stimulates mild cellular autophagy while preventing nocturnal cortisol surges.
potential_benefits: Supports circadian melatonin and insulin rhythm
Improves morning energy and mental clarity

keyBenefits: Gentle 14-hour overnight fasting window (e.g. 8:00 PM to 10:00 AM)
10-hour feeding window with 2 nourishing meals and 1 snack
Zero disruption to thyroid or reproductive axes
allowedFoods: During Fast: Plain water, Spearmint tea, Black coffee without sugar
During Window: Red rice, Fish, Eggs, Vegetables, Lentils, Nuts
guidelines: Finish your last meal of the day by 8:00 PM.
Break your fast at 10:00 AM the next morning with protein and healthy fats rather than pure carbs.
Stay well hydrated with plain water and unsweetened herbal tea during the fasting window.

sampleMealDay.breakfast: 10:00 AM (Break Fast): 2 boiled eggs + 1 cup warm spearmint tea + 10 almonds
sampleMealDay.lunch: 1:30 PM: 1 cup Red rice + Katla fish curry + Palong shak bhaji + Cucumber salad
sampleMealDay.dinner: 7:30 PM (Last Meal): 2 multigrain rotis + Chicken curry + Steamed vegetables with lemon
sampleMealDay.snack: 4:30 PM: 1 cup Tok doi with chia seeds and cinnamon

diet_plans.name: Gut-Healing & Anti-Bloat Protocol
diet_plans.tagline: Gentle digestive nutrition featuring live probiotics, soothing broths, and soluble fibers
diet_plans.description: Alleviates abdominal distension, gas, and irregular bowel habits through easily digestible local foods.
diet_plans.fullOverview: Dysbiosis, sluggish motility, or IBS can cause persistent bloating. This protocol features traditional Bangladeshi fermented Tok doi (live culture yogurt), green papaya (papain enzymes), bone broths, and isabgol.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Individuals experiencing abdominal bloating, indigestion, or irritable bowel patterns

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: Live lactobacilli in Tok doi support microbiome diversity, while soluble fibers (isabgol, pectin) normalize stool form without excessive fermentation gas.
potential_benefits: Reduces postprandial abdominal fullness and bloating

keyBenefits: Natural live probiotic cultures from Bangladeshi Tok doi
Digestive enzymes from raw/cooked green papaya (Kacha pepe)
Soothing, low-grease light fish curries (Patla jhol)
foodsToLimit: Heavy raw cabbage/beans in large quantities
guidelines: Consume 1/2 cup of fresh Tok doi with lunch every day for beneficial lactic acid bacteria.
Eat cooked green papaya (pepe) or bottle gourd (lau) 3-4 times weekly for smooth digestion.
Take 1 tsp isabgol in a glass of water before bedtime for gentle motility support.

sampleMealDay.breakfast: Warm rolled oats cooked in water with 1 tbsp Tok doi and sliced ripe papaya + 1 boiled egg
sampleMealDay.lunch: 1 cup soft cooked rice + Light Shing fish and green papaya broth (Pepe diye shing macher patla jhol) + 1/2 cup Tok doi
sampleMealDay.dinner: 1 soft handmade roti + Boiled bottle gourd and carrot curry + Shredded boiled chicken
sampleMealDay.snack: 1 cup warm ginger mint tea + 1 tsp isabgol in water

diet_plans.name: High-Protein Muscle Recomposition Protocol
diet_plans.tagline: High-protein nutritional protocol to support lean muscle retention and fat reduction
diet_plans.description: Supplies 1.6g - 2.0g protein per kg bodyweight alongside resistance training to reshape body composition.
diet_plans.fullOverview: Designed for individuals looking to shed adipose tissue while preserving or building metabolic lean mass. Features lean deshi chicken breast, egg whites, fish, besan, and lentils.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Individuals engaging in resistance training or seeking lean body recomposition

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: Higher protein intake elevates muscle protein synthesis (MPS) via leucine-mediated mTOR signaling and increases the thermic effect of food (TEF).
potential_benefits: Supports skeletal muscle hypertrophy and retention

keyBenefits: 40% of total calories from quality, high-biological-value protein
Timed carbohydrates around workout sessions for performance
Satiety-enhancing fiber from whole vegetables
foodsToLimit: Sugary protein bars with artificial syrups
guidelines: Distribute your protein evenly across 3-4 meals (25g-35g protein per feeding).
Consume your primary carbohydrate portion within 2 hours before or after your workout session.
Drink at least 3.0 liters of water daily to support amino acid metabolism and kidney filtration.

sampleMealDay.breakfast: 4 egg whites + 1 whole egg scrambled + 2 slices whole wheat toast + Black coffee
sampleMealDay.lunch: 150g grilled chicken breast + 1 cup Red rice + 1 bowl mixed dal + Sautéed green beans
sampleMealDay.dinner: 150g Rui fish steak + 1 large bowl broccoli and carrot stir-fry + 1 small roti
sampleMealDay.snack: 1 cup hung Tok doi (Greek style) with 1 scoop protein powder or 1 tbsp peanut butter

diet_plans.name: Plant-Forward Estrogen Balance Protocol
diet_plans.tagline: Cruciferous compounds and dietary lignans to support Phase I and Phase II estrogen metabolism
diet_plans.description: Features cooked Brassica vegetables, ground flaxseeds, and fiber to support normal estrogen clearance.
diet_plans.fullOverview: Estrogen dominance can contribute to heavy menstrual bleeding and breast tenderness. This plant-forward protocol supplies indole-3-carbinol (I3C), DIM, and lignans to support 2-hydroxyestrone metabolic clearance.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Individuals seeking nutritional support for estrogen metabolism and heavy cycles

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: Indole-3-carbinol (I3C) in Brassicas promotes the less estrogenic 2-hydroxyestrone pathway over 16-alpha-hydroxyestrone, while flax lignans bind excess circulating estrogen.
potential_benefits: Aids in reducing cyclical breast discomfort
Promotes healthy daily bowel elimination of bound estrogens

keyBenefits: Rich in dietary lignans from fresh ground flaxseeds (Tisi)
Cruciferous phytonutrients (DIM/I3C) for liver cytochrome support
Very high dietary fiber to prevent intestinal estrogen reabsorption
guidelines: Take 1 tablespoon of freshly ground flaxseeds (tisi) daily with your morning oats or yogurt.
Eat 1 cup of cooked cruciferous vegetables (broccoli/cauliflower) daily.
Maintain regular daily bowel movements to prevent beta-glucuronidase deconjugation of estrogen.

sampleMealDay.breakfast: 1 bowl oats with 1 tbsp ground flaxseeds + 1 cup soy/almond milk + Sliced green apple
sampleMealDay.lunch: 1 cup Red rice + Cooked broccoli and chickpea curry + Sautéed Palong shak + Raw grated carrot salad
sampleMealDay.dinner: Grilled tofu or light fish steak + Steamed cauliflower and green beans + 1 small roti
sampleMealDay.snack: A handful of roasted pumpkin seeds + 1 cup unsweetened green tea

diet_plans.name: Deshi Iron & Hemoglobin Booster Protocol
diet_plans.tagline: Bioavailable heme and non-heme iron paired with Vitamin C to support hemoglobin synthesis
diet_plans.description: Combines iron-dense deshi foods with natural ascorbic acid enhancers while avoiding iron absorption inhibitors.
diet_plans.fullOverview: Iron deficiency anemia leads to chronic fatigue, pallor, and hair thinning. This protocol pairs organic liver, green bananas (Kanchakola), amla (Amroki), and lemon with meals while separating tea/coffee by 2 hours.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Individuals with low ferritin, borderline hemoglobin (<12 g/dL), or postpartum blood loss

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) reduces non-heme ferric iron (Fe3+) to the soluble ferrous form (Fe2+), facilitating duodenal DMT-1 transporter uptake.
potential_benefits: Supports red blood cell hemoglobin production
Aids hair retention and nail strength

keyBenefits: High heme and non-heme iron from local deshi sources
Vitamin C pairing (Lemon, Amla, Guava) at every main meal
Strict separation of tea/coffee tannins from meal times
foodsToLimit: Drinking tea or coffee within 90 minutes of lunch/dinner
Antacids taken directly with iron-rich foods
guidelines: Always squeeze half a fresh lemon onto your dal and vegetable plate to double iron absorption.
Never drink milk tea or black coffee right after lunch; wait at least 90-120 minutes.
Eat 2-3 Medjool or deshi dates along with 1 fresh amla in the afternoon.

sampleMealDay.breakfast: 2 whole eggs scrambled with tomatoes + 1 slice whole wheat bread + 1 glass orange/amla juice
sampleMealDay.lunch: 1 cup Red rice + Chicken liver curry (Kolija) or Shing fish + Kanchakola bhaji + Squeezed lemon on dal
sampleMealDay.dinner: 2 rotis + Palong shak and paneer/tofu curry + 1 bowl lentil soup with lemon slice
sampleMealDay.snack: 3 dates + 1 fresh guava (rich in Vitamin C) + 1 glass water

diet_plans.name: Postpartum & Lactation Recovery Protocol
diet_plans.tagline: Nutrient-rich galactagogue and tissue recovery protocol for nursing mothers
diet_plans.description: Supports breast milk volume and maternal tissue healing using traditional deshi galactagogues.
diet_plans.fullOverview: Postpartum recovery requires additional caloric and micronutrient support for tissue repair and breast milk synthesis. This protocol features black seed (Kalo jira), moringa leaves (Sojne pata), oats, and nourishing broths.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Nursing mothers seeking healthy milk production and postpartum physical recovery

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: Beta-glucans in oats and phytochemicals in black seed and moringa stimulate prolactin release and provide dense calcium, iron, and protein for lactation.
potential_benefits: Accelerates maternal tissue and pelvic floor recovery

keyBenefits: Natural galactagogues (Kalo jira, Sojne pata, Oats) to support prolactin
Extra 400-500 kcal allowance for healthy milk volume
High calcium and iron for postpartum repletion
allowedFoods: Black cumin seed paste (Kalo jira bhorta)
Shing and Magur fish patla jhol
foodsToLimit: Crash diets and starvation caloric deficits
guidelines: Include 1 tsp Kalo jira bhorta with your lunch rice for traditional lactation support.
Drink a glass of warm milk or water right after every nursing session to stay hydrated.
Do not attempt aggressive weight loss diets during the first 6 months of exclusive breastfeeding.

sampleMealDay.breakfast: 1 bowl warm oats cooked in milk with honey, chia seeds, and 1 boiled egg
sampleMealDay.lunch: 1.5 cups Red rice + Kalo jira bhorta + Shing fish jhol with green papaya + Sojne pata bhaji
sampleMealDay.dinner: 2 handmade rotis + Garlic chicken soup with carrots and beans + 1 cup warm milk before bed
sampleMealDay.snack: 1 cup Tok doi with sliced banana and roasted almonds

diet_plans.name: Collagen & Skin-Hair Vitality Protocol
diet_plans.tagline: Glycine-rich bone broths, Vitamin C, and silica to support dermal elasticity and hair follicles
diet_plans.description: Provides natural collagen amino acid building blocks, biotin, and antioxidants for skin elasticity and hair strength.
diet_plans.fullOverview: Dermal collagen synthesis requires prolyl-hydroxylase cofactors including Vitamin C, zinc, and amino acids. This protocol features traditional slow-simmered bone broths (Payaboro/Nehari broth), amla, guava, and pumpkin seeds.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Individuals experiencing hair thinning, dry skin, or seeking skin-connective tissue support

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: Glycine and proline from bone broths paired with Vitamin C stimulate dermal fibroblast collagen synthesis, while zinc and biotin support hair keratinization.
potential_benefits: Strengthens brittle nails and joint connective tissues

keyBenefits: Natural collagen peptides from slow-cooked bone broths
Ascorbic acid from fresh Amla and Guava for prolyl-hydroxylase activity
Biotin and Zinc from eggs and pumpkin seeds
foodsToLimit: Excessive refined sugar (which causes collagen glycation)
guidelines: Drink 1 cup of warm, well-strained bone broth 3-4 times a week.
Consume 1 fresh amla or guava daily for the necessary Vitamin C to assemble collagen fibers.
Eat a handful of raw pumpkin seeds daily for zinc and plant sterols.

sampleMealDay.breakfast: 2 whole eggs scrambled with tomatoes + 1 slice whole wheat bread + 1 fresh amla or glass of amla water
sampleMealDay.lunch: 1 cup Red rice + Rui fish curry with carrots and tomatoes + Palong shak bhaji + Cucumber salad
sampleMealDay.dinner: 1 cup warm nourishing bone broth + 1 handmade roti + Grilled chicken breast and steamed vegetables
sampleMealDay.snack: 1 cup green tea + 1 tbsp roasted pumpkin seeds and 4 walnuts

diet_plans.name: Deshi Mediterranean Longevity Protocol
diet_plans.tagline: Monounsaturated fats, colorful antioxidants, and fresh fish adapted for Bangladeshi cuisine
diet_plans.description: Combines Mediterranean heart-health principles with locally available deshi ingredients for metabolic longevity.
diet_plans.fullOverview: The Mediterranean diet is globally recognized for cardiovascular and metabolic longevity. This protocol adapts its core tenets using cold-pressed mustard/olive oil, local river fish, colorful vegetables, garlic, and lentils.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Individuals seeking long-term metabolic health, cardiovascular protection, and healthy aging

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: High polyphenol and monounsaturated fatty acid (MUFA) intake improves endothelial nitric oxide bioavailability and reduces LDL oxidation.
potential_benefits: Supports healthy lipid profiles (HDL to triglyceride ratio)
Promotes long-term cognitive and metabolic health

keyBenefits: Rich in monounsaturated fats from olive and cold-pressed mustard oil
Emphasis on fresh deshi fish, lentils, and colorful vegetables
Strong evidence base for cardiovascular and cognitive longevity
allowedFoods: Extra virgin olive oil and cold-pressed mustard oil
guidelines: Use olive oil for raw salads and cold-pressed mustard oil for light fish curries.
Eat fish at least 4-5 times a week in place of red meat.
Fill half your plate with colorful vegetables (tomatoes, spinach, beans, carrots) at lunch and dinner.

sampleMealDay.breakfast: 2 whole eggs scrambled with tomatoes and olive oil + 1 slice whole wheat bread + Green tea
sampleMealDay.lunch: 1 cup Red rice + Rui fish cooked with garlic tomato gravy + Sautéed mixed shak + Cucumber tomato salad with olive oil
sampleMealDay.dinner: 1 handmade roti + Thick mixed lentil dal with vegetables + Grilled fish fillet
sampleMealDay.snack: 1/2 cup Tok doi with a handful of walnuts and a sprinkle of cinnamon

diet_plans.name: Stress & Adrenal Nutrition Support Protocol
diet_plans.tagline: Magnesium-rich foods, adaptogenic teas, and stable complex carbohydrates to moderate stress responses
diet_plans.description: Supports adrenal function and moderates stress-induced cortisol spikes through nutrient-rich whole foods.
diet_plans.fullOverview: Chronic emotional and physical stress elevates cortisol, contributing to visceral fat accumulation, sleep disruption, and cravings. This protocol emphasizes magnesium-rich pumpkin seeds, sweet potatoes, dark chocolate, and Tulsi tea.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Individuals experiencing chronic stress, high evening anxiety, or cortisol-related belly fat

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: Magnesium acts as a natural NMDA receptor blocker and GABA agonist, while slow-digesting evening carbohydrates support serotonin and melatonin synthesis.
potential_benefits: Aids in reducing stress-related central abdominal fat

keyBenefits: Rich in dietary Magnesium and Vitamin B6 for GABA pathway support
Strategic complex carbohydrates at dinner to support sleep melatonin
Calming adaptogenic herbal teas (Tulsi and Chamomile)
guidelines: Do not drink coffee or strong black tea on an empty stomach in the morning.
Include a small boiled sweet potato or cup of warm milk with dinner to support peaceful sleep.
Drink a warm cup of Tulsi herbal tea 45 minutes before bedtime.

sampleMealDay.breakfast: 2 whole eggs scrambled with spinach + 1 slice whole wheat toast + 1 cup warm Tulsi tea

diet_plans.name: Nutritional Re-Nourish & Healthy Weight Protocol
diet_plans.tagline: Nutrient-dense, wholesome caloric surplus protocol for period recovery and lean mass
diet_plans.description: Supports hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian signaling and healthy weight restoration using nutrient-dense wholesome foods.
diet_plans.fullOverview: Hypothalamic Amenorrhea and underweight status occur when low energy availability downregulates GnRH and LH pulsatility. This protocol provides a structured 300-500 kcal surplus utilizing peanut butter, pure ghee, nuts, and banana smoothies.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Underweight individuals (BMI <18.5) or those recovering from functional hypothalamic amenorrhea

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: Restoring adequate energy availability (>45 kcal/kg fat-free mass/day) normalizes kisspeptin, leptin, and GnRH pulsatility to restore ovulatory function.
potential_benefits: Supports resumption of regular menstrual cycles
Enhances bone mineral density and thermal regulation

keyBenefits: Nutrient-dense caloric surplus without empty junk food
Healthy fats (Peanut butter, Ghee, Almonds) for steroid hormone synthesis
Frequent, easy-to-digest calorie boosters (Smoothies, Nut butter toasts)
allowedFoods: Pure Deshi Ghee (1-2 tsp with rice)
foodsToLimit: Dirty bulking with rancid street oils
Excessive volume low-calorie foods that prevent eating enough
guidelines: Add 1 tsp pure ghee or butter to your hot rice and dal at both lunch and dinner.
Drink a nourishing smoothie with whole milk, 1 banana, 1 tbsp peanut butter, and 2 dates daily.
Eat every 3 to 4 hours consistently without skipping planned meals.

diet_plans.name: PMS & PMDD Luteal Phase Nutrition Protocol
diet_plans.tagline: Magnesium, Vitamin B6, and steady-carbohydrate nutrition to support luteal phase mood and comfort
diet_plans.description: Supports serotonin synthesis and balances progesterone-to-estrogen ratios during the 10 days before menstruation.
diet_plans.fullOverview: The luteal phase demands stable blood glucose and elevated micronutrients to buffer mood swings and water retention. This protocol features sunflower seeds, chickpeas, dark chocolate, and bananas.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Individuals experiencing pre-menstrual mood changes, bloating, cramps, or intense sugar cravings

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: Vitamin B6 acts as a cofactor in decarboxylating 5-HTP to serotonin and L-DOPA to dopamine, while magnesium reduces prostaglandin-mediated uterine cramping.
potential_benefits: Moderates cyclical irritability and depressive mood dips
Reduces pre-menstrual water retention and breast tenderness

keyBenefits: Vitamin B6 and Magnesium for neurotransmitter balance
Ginger tea for prostaglandin-mediated cramp soothing
Steady complex carbohydrates to prevent hypoglycemic mood dips
foodsToLimit: Excessive salt during the premenstrual week (causes fluid retention)
guidelines: Drink 2 cups of fresh ginger tea daily during the 7 days prior to your expected period.
Snack on 1 tbsp sunflower seeds and 1 square of dark chocolate in the late afternoon.
Avoid adding extra salt to meals during the pre-menstrual week to prevent fluid puffiness.

diet_plans.name: Perimenopause & Bone Density Protocol
diet_plans.tagline: Calcium, Vitamin D, and phytoestrogenic nutrition to support bone density and vasomotor comfort
diet_plans.description: Supports bone mineral retention and vascular comfort during the perimenopausal and menopausal transition.
diet_plans.fullOverview: Declining estrogen levels accelerate bone calcium resorption and trigger vasomotor hot flashes. This protocol emphasizes small bony fish (Mola/Dhela mach), sesame seeds (Til), calcium-set tofu, and Tok doi.
diet_plans.targetAudience: Women in perimenopause or menopause (ages 40-60+) focusing on bone density and hormonal transition

evidence_profile.mechanism_summary: Supplies bioavailable calcium and phosphorus from soft-boned small fish alongside mild phytoestrogenic isoflavones to moderate estrogenic receptor decline.
potential_benefits: Helps moderate the intensity of vasomotor hot flashes

keyBenefits: High dietary Calcium from small deshi fish eaten with bones (Mola, Dhela)
Plant isoflavones (Sesame, Tofu) for gentle estrogenic receptor support
Adequate protein to prevent age-related sarcopenia
allowedFoods: Small fish eaten with soft bones (Mola, Dhela, Kholisha)
foodsToLimit: Excessively spicy foods that trigger hot flashes
High sodium foods that increase urinary calcium loss
guidelines: Eat small deshi fish with bones (Mola/Dhela) 2-3 times weekly for bioavailable calcium and phosphorus.
Incorporate 1 tablespoon of sesame seeds (Til) or 1 cup of Tok doi into your daily diet.
Engage in weight-bearing walking or light resistance exercises 3-4 days a week for bone remodeling.
